items.q: What should you remember about **Studying with ADHD**?
items.a: **Born with ADD/ADHD; bottom-of-barrel learner; rewrites same page daily until photographic memory;** Jennifer learns paramedic material while quizzing him; medications have unpronounceable names learned syllable-by-syllable. Multi-millionaire at 49 but still 4+ hr/day review because retention isn't permanent.

items.q: What should you remember about **Friction is the feature**?
items.a: **"Everything I do in life, it sucks." No passion/motivation/discipline buzzwords** — "just do." Ice bath you love → no aMCC growth; cold water you fear → growth. Must renew daily (like sobriety: cure works one day at a time).

items.q: What should you remember about **Haunted, not inspired**?
items.a: Early abuse, racism, obesity, lies-for-approval created a character he became **haunted** by; improvement isn't permanent — turn discipline off and "David Goggins that is" returns. Social media judged by people he used to be.

items.q: What should you remember about **Stick-only engine**?
items.a: **No imagining paramedic glory or book launch;** maybe/maybe carrot at best. Back-of-brain voice before every hard test: "this ain't you, bro.".

items.q: What should you remember about **Two (or many) voices**?
items.a: External criticism is "cap gun fire"; internal dialogue is worse. Multiple voices — some all wrong — but years of pinpoint practice let you ignore them and still execute. Must listen to **your journey**, not everyone else's noise.

items.q: What should you remember about **Fail first, win later**?
items.a: **Black kid, 300 lb, can't swim → Navy SEAL** = insurmountable odds → learn to fail properly or stay in the hole. Didn't talk about winning for years.

items.q: What should you remember about **Harsh mirror for obesity**?
items.a: **Won't sugar-coat for 300+ lb friends**: maybe you like the horror film you're living; tiny internal flame required — can't light it for you. Weight loss sucks every day (Indiana cold, injuries, more suck).

items.q: What should you remember about **Unseen work / medicine cabinet**?
items.a: Real passion is daily unseen reps, not stage passion. Brain = most powerful weapon; right internal dialogue + proof of past reps → "beast." End state: always **found**, never lost — journey doesn't get easier.
**Brutal honesty; stopped people-pleasing; partner Jennifer sees** the real process. Self-reflection in cupboards (Huberman + Paul Conti: unconscious = supercomputer; introspection required).

items.q: What should you remember about **Perishable skills**?
items.a: Even SEALs don't want to return to the suck; Goggins **must** go back — that's where all knowledge lives.
